newsitem.title: INDIA: Doctors say Mother Teresa unstable, postpone X-ray.
newsitem.headline: Doctors say Mother Teresa unstable, postpone X-ray.

text.p: Doctors treating Mother Teresa at an Indian heart clinic said on Tuesday her condition was unstable and postponed a planned X-ray to see if surgery was needed.

"We have to postpone the angiography for a couple of days because she is clinically unstable," Dr Tarun Praharaj, a member of her medical team at the B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre in Calcutta, told Reuters.
He said the condition of the 86-year-old Roman Catholic nun, known as the "Saint of the Gutters" for her work with the world's downtrodden, could "turn bad any moment".

"She is cheerful and talking but she is having heart failures and we don't know when she will have her next chest pain... We have to make her more comfortable before we go for angiography," Praharaj added late on Tuesday.

Mother Teresa was moved earlier in the day from intensive care at the Woodlands Nursing Home to the nearby clinic, where doctors had said an angiography -- an X-ray of blood vessels to detect any blocked artery -- might take place on Wednesday.
She was admitted to the nursing home early on Friday with an irregular heartbeat.
Mother Teresa, fitted with a heart pacemaker in 1989, twice has undergone coronary angiography -- in the United States in 1991 and at the Birla clinic in 1993.
In both cases she subsequently underwent angioplasty, in which surgeons inserted a balloon into her artery to unblock it.

Earlier on Tuesday, a hushed crowd of about 200 people, including nuns from her Missionaries of Charity religious order, watched Mother Teresa, eyes shut and arms folded over her chest, as she was carried from the nursing home on a stretcher.
A doctor, a nurse and four nuns escorted her in the ambulance on the short drive to the heart clinic.
"Generally she is all right," said A.K. Chatterjee, the heart clinic administrator, said later.
"She has been placed in the critical care unit, where all heart support arrangements are available," he added.
Dr S.K. Sen, of the Woodlands Nursing Home, told reporters Mother Teresa had another bout of chest pain on Tuesday afternoon, which briefly delayed her transfer to the clinic.
Dr Patricia Aubanel, who treated her in the United States, had arrived in Calcutta to supervise the procedure, he added.
Mother Teresa, who has ischaemia, or hardening of the arteries, had suffered heart failure several times since last Thursday.
But on Monday she had shown some reluctance to undergo any special tests or surgery.
Sen said on Tuesday she had agreed to undergo angiography, which he described as a very safe procedure involving the injection of dye through a catheter.
The dye shows up on the X-ray, revealing any blockage. The patient will be put under general anaesthesia, he said.
Sen said the two doctors who performed angioplasty on Mother Teresa at the Birla centre in 1993 -- Praharaj and Deepak Shetty -- would conduct the angiography.
